pr.title: Add a test for FileNameResolver
pr.author: olha
pr.body: The resolver had no test. Now a test uses a fresh temp folder and checks two reservations of the same name. It removes the folder at the end.

explain: Good test. Each test has its own unique folder (uniqid), so tests do not collide with each other or with real files. tearDown cleans up. It tests the real class and its main rule, not a mock. Approve.

title: Senior asks: a.tar.csv is already in storage/. A user uploads a.tar.csv again. Which name does reserveFreeName() give? (What does this print?)
explain: pathinfo() cuts only the last dot. PATHINFO_FILENAME gives a.tar and the extension is csv. The code builds name + _1 + . + extension: a.tar_1.csv. Files without an extension are the odd case: the name becomes README_1. with a dot at the end. Think about it when you review.

title: Senior asks: upload() reserves a free name first, then calls move_uploaded_file(). The move fails (disk full). What is left in storage/?
options: An empty file with the reserved name
Nothing. PHP removes the file by itself
A half-written file with the real data
explain: reserveFreeName() already created an empty file with fopen('x'). If the move fails, nobody removes it, so an empty file stays. read() on it later gives an error. Fix: delete the reserved file in a catch or when move_uploaded_file() returns false, before you throw StorageException.

title: Senior asks: a user saves fruits.csv from Excel as UTF-8. The file starts with a BOM (hidden bytes EF BB BF). The first header is id. Does $row['id'] exist after read()?
options: No. The first key is 'id' with the BOM in front, so it is another string
Yes. PHP removes the BOM when it reads a CSV
The read() call throws a JsonException
explain: PHP does not strip the BOM. The first header becomes "\u{FEFF}id", which looks the same on screen but is not equal to 'id'. So the page shows empty ids. Fix: remove the BOM from the first header (or from the start of the file) when you read.

title: A checkbox #agree starts unchecked. The user clicks it. Which call tells you the current state?
explain: The checked attribute is the start value from the HTML. It does not change when the user clicks. The checked property is the live state: true or false. Use .prop() for checked, disabled and selected. Use .attr() for things like href or data in the HTML.

title: You add a package to composer.json by hand. Then you run composer install. What happens?
options: Composer warns that the lock file is not up to date, and installs from composer.lock. The new package is missing
Composer adds the package and updates composer.lock
Composer fails and installs nothing at all
explain: install reads composer.lock, not composer.json. If they do not match, you get a warning and the new package is not installed. Use composer require vendor/package. It edits composer.json, updates composer.lock and installs, all in one step.

title: PHP 8.1. What does this print?
explain: tryFrom() returns null when no case has that value. from() would throw a ValueError. Use tryFrom for user input and handle the null. ->name is the case name (Open), ->value is the stored string (open).
code:
<?php
enum Status: string {
    case Open = 'open';
    case Closed = 'closed';
}

var_dump(Status::tryFrom('done'));
echo Status::from('open')->name;

title: You changed app.php by mistake. Nothing is committed or staged. You want the old content back. Which command?
explain: git restore <file> replaces the file with the last committed version. Your edits are lost, so be sure. git revert makes a new commit that undoes an old commit. git reset --soft moves the branch, not file content.
